videos.script: Lívia's first week at Varanda opened with four questions. {{four}} How much did we sell last year? Why did October fall? How much will we sell this quarter? When should the warehouse reorder? They sound alike. They are four different kinds of work. {{timeline}} The first looks at the past and counts it. The second looks at the past and explains it. The third looks ahead. The fourth chooses what to do. This lesson is the first kind, descriptive analysis, and it is the one the other three stand on. {{sheet}} You type Varanda's two years, month by month, and compare them two ways. Against the month before, the numbers swing by as much as 26 per cent and mean almost nothing. Against the same month a year before, one month stands out. {{growth}} Then the arithmetic of growth, where correct sums give wrong sentences: an average that is not the year, and a share that rose by 0.3 points and by 2.6 per cent at once. {{report}} Last, the report itself. Five parts, one sentence of finding, and one thing it must not do: explain October before anybody has checked.
